item.title: NGINX CVE-2026-123633 HTTP/2 Flaw and ARTEX Hunting Guidance
item.content:encoded:
Window: 24 Nov 23:00 → 25 Nov 03:00 UTC (4 hours)

NGINX HTTP/2 Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-123633 — Must Read

CVE-2026-123633 is a critical NGINX HTTP/2 use-after-free affecting reverse proxies under worker-connection pressure, enabling unauthenticated denial of service and potentially code execution if ASLR is bypassed. Upgrade to NGINX 1.30.7 or 1.31.9 (or a vendor-backported fixed package) and review exposed HTTP/2 proxy configurations.

  • CVE-2026-123633 is an HTTP/2 use-after-free flaw in NGINX that can let an unauthenticated attacker cause a denial of service when a reverse proxy is low on available worker connections.
  • Affected versions are NGINX 1.19.7 through 1.30.6 and 1.31.0 through 1.31.8, while NGINX 1.30.7 and 1.31.9 contain the fix.
  • The defect can leave an active HTTP/2 request marked as reusable, allowing NGINX to close its connection and free memory still used by the request under connection pressure.
  • The researcher reproduced a read from freed DNS resolver memory using AddressSanitizer on NGINX 1.31.7 and 1.31.8 in an isolated Debian test environment.
  • F5 states that code execution may be possible when address space layout randomization is disabled or bypassed, and recommends upgrading to a fixed release or vendor package containing the fix.

Technologies: web-server, proxy, load-balancer

Products: nginx, nginx-plus

Vendors: f5, palo-alto-networks

Detecting and hunting ARTEX with Corelight | Corelight — Optional

Corelight provides guidance for detecting and hunting ARTEX activity using network evidence, with a focus on identifying suspicious Windows Task Scheduler behavior and related indicators.

  • The article is titled “Detecting and hunting ARTEX with Corelight.”
  • The article concerns detecting ARTEX activity.
  • The article discusses hunting for ARTEX using Corelight.

Technologies: network-monitoring

Products: windows-task-scheduler

Vendors: corelight, microsoft

item.title: Rackspace Spot Shutdown, Colorado myColorado Breach, and Inception Vishing Campaign
item.content:encoded:
Window: 24 Nov 19:00 → 24 Nov 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

New Inception extortion gang launches large-scale vishing campaign — Should Read

The new Inception extortion group is running a large-scale phone-based phishing campaign using fake Okta and OpenText authentication sites to steal corporate SSO credentials. Researchers and Okta assess it is likely a rebrand of a ShinyHunters-linked cluster, though Inception denies the connection.

  • The newly formed Inception extortion group has been linked to a large-scale campaign targeting single sign-on credentials through phone-based social engineering and fake authentication websites.
  • Inception appeared publicly on November 17 and claimed seven victims, including AMD, PepsiCo, Cigna Healthcare, AutoZone, and Lucid Motors, although none has publicly confirmed a data breach.
  • ReversingLabs identified 21 domains used for single sign-on phishing, 41 domains believed to support the campaign infrastructure, and four additional suspicious domains.
  • Okta assessed that Inception is very likely a rebranding of O-UNC-053, a threat cluster previously associated with ShinyHunters, based on consistent infrastructure and tactics.
  • ReversingLabs recommends phishing-resistant sign-in methods such as FIDO2 security keys and passkeys, stronger help desk identity checks, and review of relevant logs dating to October 21, 2026.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam

Products: opentext-access-manager

Vendors: okta, opentext, reversinglabs

Rackspace shuts down Spot cloud platform after security breach — Should Read

Rackspace will permanently shut down its Rackspace Spot cloud platform on December 8, 2026, after compromised credentials let attackers access customer Kubernetes clusters, secrets, and storage files. Customers must migrate workloads and rotate potentially exposed tokens, kubeconfigs, and Kubernetes Secrets.

  • Rackspace will permanently discontinue its Rackspace Spot cloud platform on December 8, 2026, at 5 PM Central Time, after which remaining workloads will be terminated and customer data will no longer be accessible.
  • The company decided to wind down Rackspace Spot after attackers used compromised credentials on November 17 to access customer Kubernetes clusters and potentially read secrets and files on storage volumes.
  • Rackspace discovered the intrusion on November 18 after a customer report, disabled the platform administration console, and restored service on November 21.
  • Rackspace advises all Spot customers to treat API tokens, refresh tokens, kubeconfigs, and Kubernetes Secrets as potentially compromised and to review access logs beginning November 16.
  • Rackspace says the affected Spot environment is segmented from its core infrastructure and that it found no evidence of unauthorized access to its core systems or other Rackspace customer environments.

Technologies: cloud-platform, container-platform, orchestration, secrets-manager

Products: rackspace-spot, kubernetes

Vendors: rackspace, kubernetes

Colorado says cyberattack took down myColorado app, warns 150,000 had data stolen — Should Read

Colorado’s myColorado app was taken offline after a cyberattack discovered November 18, with state officials warning that data linked to nearly 150,000 of its 2.1 million users may have been stolen. Residents must use physical IDs and agency websites while the state investigates and restores the service.

  • Colorado’s Governor’s Office of Information Technology said it discovered a cyberattack involving the myColorado app on the evening of November 18 and shut the app down.
  • The state said data connected to nearly 150,000 people may have been stolen, though investigators did not specify what information was involved.
  • myColorado has 2.1 million users and provides digital identification, document storage, and access to state government services.
  • Colorado advised residents traveling for Thanksgiving to carry physical identification, while state services remain available through agency websites.
  • The Gentlemen ransomware group claimed responsibility for the incident on Sunday.

Products: mycolorado

California privacy agency director Kemp to leave after two-year tenure — May Read

California Privacy Protection Agency Executive Director Tom Kemp will depart after nearly two years, during which the agency launched its consumer data-deletion and opt-out platform used by more than 600,000 Californians.

  • California Privacy Protection Agency Executive Director Tom Kemp announced that he will leave the agency after nearly two years leading it.
  • Kemp highlighted the Delete Request and Opt-Out Platform, which launched in January and is used by more than 600,000 Californians to block data sharing and request deletions from data brokers.
  • According to Kemp, each user of the platform has prompted more than 200 data deletions by data brokers on average.
  • Penalties for companies that violate consumers’ privacy choices through the platform took effect in August.
  • During Kemp’s tenure, the agency issued its largest fine, promoted two privacy-expansion laws, and adopted regulations for cybersecurity audits, risk assessments, and automated decision-making technology.

Products: delete-request-and-opt-out-platform

Vendors: california-privacy-protection-agency

item.title: ARTEX AI Attacks, Check Point GT13 Intrusions, and Radware Cloud-Key Exposure
item.content:encoded:
Window: 24 Nov 15:00 → 24 Nov 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hackers compromise Check Point Servers in 22 organizations — Must Read

GreyNoise found an ongoing campaign compromising 24 Check Point Security Management servers across 22 organizations, with attackers stealing sensitive firewall data, disabling policies, and attempting lateral movement. The initial access vector is unknown, but attackers abused the actively exploited Check Point SmartConsole authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-16232 after compromise.

  • GreyNoise tracked an intrusion campaign called GT13 that compromised 24 Check Point Security Management servers at 22 organizations across 17 countries between October 17 and November 2.
  • The affected organizations include government entities, financial services providers, and companies in the energy, transportation, mining, and manufacturing sectors.
  • The attackers stole firewall databases, credentials, configuration data, and internal certificate authority files, and they also unloaded security policies in some cases.
  • GreyNoise observed post-compromise exploitation of CVE-2026-16232, a Check Point SmartConsole authentication bypass that can provide administrator-level access.
  • The attackers conducted internal reconnaissance and attempted to move to additional systems including Citrix NetScaler, Ivanti Connect Secure, VMware vCenter, Microsoft Exchange, and Microsoft Netlogon.

Technologies: firewall, web-server, load-balancer, remote-access, hypervisor, operating-system

Products: check-point-security-management-server, smartconsole, rejetto-http-file-server, citrix-netscaler, ivanti-connect-secure, vmware-vcenter, microsoft-exchange

Vendors: check-point, rejetto, citrix, ivanti, vmware, microsoft, expressvpn, greynoise

Lawmakers warn ID verification companies to bolster security after September hack — Should Read

U.S. lawmakers urged identity-verification companies to strengthen data security after an IDScan breach exposed scans of more than 150 million IDs, which were later offered on the Nexus dark-web marketplace. The incident highlights the persistent fraud and national-security risks of retaining detailed identity documents.

  • A bipartisan group of six federal lawmakers sent letters to identity verification companies seeking details on how they handle and protect customers’ sensitive data after the September IDScan breach.
  • The IDScan breach exposed scans of more than 150 million driver’s licenses and other identification documents, along with nearly 600,000 medical cards, employment authorizations, and other sensitive records.
  • The stolen IDScan data was offered for sale on the Russia-linked Nexus dark-web marketplace, and the FBI opened an investigation.
  • The lawmakers warned that the exposed information could enable identity theft and fraud and included documents belonging to high-ranking military and intelligence officials.
  • The letters urged companies to search proactively for weaknesses, use a system in which access is not automatically trusted, and reduce how much personally identifying information they collect, share, and retain.

Technologies: iam

Vendors: idscan

Recent Trends and Tactics of Agentic AI Attacks — Should Read

Unit 42 reports that attackers are using autonomous AI agents after gaining web-shell access to rapidly perform reconnaissance, credential theft, privilege escalation and lateral movement across Linux, Windows and cloud environments. The core risk is not novel techniques but machine-speed, adaptive execution, though the agents often leave detectable clues such as high command volume, structured output delimiters and reasoning-style code comments.

  • Unit 42 reported tracking more than 10 global campaigns between July and September 2026 in which attackers used autonomous AI agents after obtaining access through web shells deployed on vulnerable web applications.
  • The observed agents performed reconnaissance, credential harvesting, privilege escalation and lateral movement, often under high-level human direction while autonomously selecting and adapting tactical steps.
  • In one investigated intrusion, an AI agent executed about 800 unique commands during 140 minutes of activity, while another campaign involved more than 8,000 unique commands over 12 days.
  • The agents moved across Linux, Windows and cloud environments, including an incident in which an agent adapted from blocked AWS IMDSv1 access to successful IMDSv2 token acquisition and then enumerated AWS services across eight regions.
  • Unit 42 identified behavioral signs that may help defenders recognize agent-driven activity, including unusually rapid command execution, structured output headers, highly varied Base64-encoded payloads and reasoning-style comments embedded in scripts.

Technologies: xdr, edr, cloud-platform, source-control, web-server

Products: cortex-xdr, cortex-xsiam, cyberstrikeai, amazon-ec2, microsoft-defender-for-endpoint, gitlab, nginx, internet-information-services

Vendors: palo-alto-networks, amazon-web-services, microsoft, gitlab

Radware discloses breach exposing customer cloud access keys — Should Read

Radware disclosed that an unauthenticated internal Cloud WAF management API exposed online allowed attackers to access some customer contact details and log-export credentials, including AWS, Azure, and SFTP keys. Affected customers should rotate those credentials and review storage-access logs for suspicious activity since November 19.

  • Radware said an unauthorized party accessed an internal Cloud WAF management API that was publicly reachable without authentication on November 19, 2026.
  • Potentially exposed information included customer contact details and, for some customers, credentials for exporting logs to AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, or SFTP storage.
  • Radware blocked the originating IP address, restricted access to the management API, and revoked and replaced all internal account credentials after detecting the incident.
  • Radware strongly advised affected WAF and bot-protection customers to rotate log-export credentials and review their cloud-storage access logs for unexpected activity since November 19.
  • Radware said it found no evidence that customer security policies or application traffic were accessed, and that WAF inspection and protection continued without interruption.

Technologies: waf, cloud-platform, object-storage

Products: radware-cloud-waf, amazon-s3, azure-blob-storage

Vendors: radware, amazon-web-services, microsoft

Iran-Aligned Volant Manticore Uses IPFS-Based KuboShell Backdoor in Espionage Campaigns — Should Read

Check Point identified Volant Manticore, an Iran-aligned espionage group likely linked to former MuddyWater operators, targeting organizations in Cyprus and Saudi Arabia. Its KuboShell backdoor uses IPFS and Pinata for command-and-control before deploying the more capable Homa framework and legitimate RMM tools.

  • Check Point identified a previously undocumented Iran-aligned espionage group called Volant Manticore that has targeted telecommunications companies, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus since at least late August 2025.
  • Volant Manticore uses the Windows backdoor KuboShell, which communicates through IPFS and Pinata to retrieve commands and return execution results.
  • The group has used AI-generated personas in fake CVs and healthcare-themed phishing ZIP archives to deliver KuboShell, Homa, and remote monitoring and management tools.
  • Check Point assesses that Volant Manticore may consist of former MuddyWater operators operating separately while retaining older MuddyWater tooling, including a JavaScript reimplementation of MuddyC2Go.
  • The group targeted Saudi Arabian healthcare entities in campaigns observed as recently as September 2026, including emails sent from a compromised account belonging to a private Saudi hospital.

Technologies: object-storage, remote-access

Products: pinata, n-able-rmm, meshcentral

Vendors: check-point, pinata, n-able, meshcentral

Turnitin discloses cyberattack affecting customer-facing systems — Should Read

Turnitin disclosed unauthorized activity on certain customer-facing systems and is investigating with external cybersecurity specialists while notifying law enforcement and regulators. The company says services remain operational, but has not disclosed whether data was accessed, the incident’s scope, or the number of people affected.

  • Turnitin disclosed unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing systems and activated its incident response plan.
  • The company is investigating with external cybersecurity specialists and says it notified law enforcement and cyber regulators.
  • Turnitin says its systems remain operational and that the affected systems do not collect government identification credentials or institutional financial information.
  • The company has not disclosed whether user data was accessed or stolen, when the incident occurred, or how many people may have been affected.
  • Turnitin's status page showed no incidents or service disruptions in November 2026, and no ransomware group had publicly claimed responsibility at the time of reporting.

Products: turnitin

Vendors: turnitin

ShinyHunters claims to return after FBI arrests, uses old PGP keys as proof — Should Read

ShinyHunters claims it has resumed operations after arrests of alleged members, launching a new Tor leak site and using historical PGP keys to support its identity. The signatures show access to old group keys but do not conclusively prove the original operators are behind the comeback.

  • ShinyHunters claims to have returned through a new Tor-based data leak site following arrests of several people reportedly linked to the group.
  • The new site published Russian and English messages and said it will communicate only through its Exploit forum account and the new Tor site.
  • The operators signed verification messages with two historical ShinyHunters PGP keys from 2020, and BleepingComputer verified the signatures.
  • The old signing keys show that the site operators can access keys historically used by ShinyHunters, but they do not prove that the original group members are operating the new site.
  • The operators said they rotated a PGP key reportedly used by Rey, who they say was arrested and is cooperating with authorities, and plan to use a new CDN for stolen data.

Carnegie Endowment for International Peace says third-party breach leaked donation info — May Read

A breach at nonprofit fundraising vendor Soapbox Engage exposed some Carnegie Endowment for International Peace donors’ names, contact details, and giving histories, though no full credit card numbers were affected. The incident is part of a recent wave of attacks targeting digital fundraising platforms.

  • Carnegie Endowment for International Peace said a cyberattack on its fundraising vendor Soapbox Engage led to unauthorized access to a small percentage of Carnegie’s database.
  • The incident occurred on October 28, and Carnegie said the unauthorized users were removed from the vendor’s systems on October 30.
  • The exposed information included donors’ names, email addresses, phone numbers, and giving histories, while no full credit card numbers were exposed.
  • Carnegie notified everyone in its database about the incident because of European data privacy laws, though it did not disclose how many people were affected.
  • DonorPerfect and GoFundMe also recently disclosed security incidents involving their fundraising platforms.

Products: soapbox-engage, donorperfect

Vendors: soapbox-engage, donorperfect, gofundme

Police disrupt 57 illegal streaming services with 7.3 million visits — May Read

A coordinated law-enforcement operation across 11 countries disrupted 57 illegal IPTV services and identified 321 piracy websites with more than 7.3 million annual visits. Investigators traced over €26 million in cryptocurrency transactions while targeting the financial networks behind the billion-euro illegal streaming market.

  • Law-enforcement authorities from 11 countries disrupted 57 illegal IPTV services and identified 321 websites offering copyrighted content without authorization.
  • The identified websites had a combined annual traffic of more than 7.3 million visits, according to Europol.
  • Investigators traced more than €26 million in cryptocurrency transactions while examining payment networks connected to the streaming services.
  • Europol, the EU Intellectual Property Office, INTERPOL, the Audiovisual Anti-Piracy Alliance, Binance, Coinbase, and Chainalysis participated in the joint action.
  • The Audiovisual Anti-Piracy Alliance estimates that legitimate providers lose about €4.83 billion annually because roughly 60 million people in Europe use illegal streaming platforms.

Vendors: binance, coinbase, chainalysis

AI Agents vs Experts: What the Data Says for 2027 — Optional

NetSPI’s EchoBench testing found that AI pentesting agents still trail trained human testers, particularly on moderate issues, injection flaws, login weaknesses, and contextual attack reasoning. The strongest approach is human-in-the-loop testing: agents broaden discovery and evidence collection while experts validate findings, assess impact, and manage false-positive review volume.

  • NetSPI’s EchoBench benchmark compared AI pentesting configurations with 425 assessments conducted by 88 trained pentesters across five web applications.
  • Experts outperformed the open-source AI setups by an average of 23 percentage points, and the gap increased from 22 points on easy issues to 30 points on moderate issues.
  • The best tested model configuration, Opus 4.7 with harness support, found 44.4% of known issue types, compared with the human baseline of 49.4%.
  • Human testers found injection flaws and login flaws more often than agents, while agents performed better on cryptographic failures and frequently identified an exposed WSDL file on one public application.
  • On every application reviewed, combining a human pentester with a typical agent run found more known issue types than either the human or agent alone.

Products: echobench, sara, cai, pentestgpt, pentestswarm, opencode, claude-opus-4-7

Vendors: netspi, synack, anthropic

ARTEX needs nine minutes. How long do your logs need? — Optional

ARTEX-style AI pentest agents do not use novel attack techniques, but they can automate reconnaissance and secret-sweeping fast enough to complete a campaign in minutes. Defenders need real-time visibility into denied cloud requests and AI model calls, since delayed log analysis will miss these short-lived operations.

  • A real ARTEX session observed by the authors lasted about nine minutes, made roughly 20 requests through five Tor exit nodes, and ended with a sweep for secrets.
  • ARTEX uses a planner agent and worker agents that run model-generated shell commands, rather than containing fixed cloud-attack logic.
  • In an AWS lab account with no credentials or website, ARTEX ran more than 2,000 tools and made only one logged request to the account: an anonymous, denied bucket-listing attempt.
  • The article says failed probes are often denied requests, so detections that exclude denied activity can miss AI-agent reconnaissance.
  • The authors argue that real-time log ingestion and immediate alert assessment are necessary because an AI-driven attack can be completed before hourly or daily log processing occurs.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, iam, container-platform

Products: artex, full-chain-sentinel, amazon-bedrock, amazon-s3

Vendors: amazon, mitiga, microsoft, connectwise, github

What the ARTEX attacks tell defenders about AI pentesting — Optional

ARTEX shows how AI-agent frameworks can rapidly scale attacks using familiar weaknesses such as exposed credentials, unauthenticated APIs, IDORs, and injection flaws. Defenders should inventory all internet-facing systems, continuously test each release within tightly controlled scope, and fix findings quickly while maintaining MFA, credential rotation, and secret-management practices.

  • ARTEX is an open-source framework that coordinates AI agents for penetration testing, but the FBI says criminals have used it against organizations since at least August.
  • Reported ARTEX-linked activity included attacks on financial institutions in South Korea, attempted sign-ins to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, and breaches disclosed by Barracuda and WorkOS.
  • The initial-access weaknesses cited in the article include hardcoded administrator passwords in JavaScript, unauthenticated APIs, insecure direct object references, command and template injection, weak administrator credentials, and stolen, exposed, or unrevoked credentials.
  • Microsoft said some intrusions progressed from selecting a target to obtaining privileged access in under three hours, making the speed of finding and fixing issues especially important.
  • The article advises defenders to inventory all internet-facing applications, test applications and external networks regularly, enforce testing scope outside the AI model, and retain MFA, credential rotation, and secret-management practices.

Technologies: identity-provider, mfa, source-control

Products: artex, cyberstrikeai, pentagi, hexstrike, microsoft-365, connectwise

Vendors: aikido-security, microsoft, amazon-web-services, crowdstrike, google, connectwise

From Vulnerability Noise to Resilience: Rethinking Security in the AI Era — Optional

RapidFort argues that AI-driven software development increases supply-chain complexity, so organizations should prioritize runtime reachability and exploitability over raw CVE counts. The sponsored article advocates automated hardening, curated container images, runtime profiling, and continuous rebuilding in CI/CD to reduce attack surface.

  • Modern containerized applications include operating systems, packages, libraries, frameworks, and dependencies, while the code written by an organization may be only a small portion of what it ships.
  • The article argues that vulnerability severity scores alone are insufficient for prioritization because teams should consider whether vulnerable code is running, reachable, exposed, known to be exploited, automatable, and likely to have meaningful technical impact.
  • A software bill of materials identifies included components, while a runtime bill of materials identifies components actually being used; the article cites an NGINX image with 152 packages and 48 CVEs in which only 47 packages were running.
  • The article recommends removing unneeded libraries, shells, package managers, build tools, and other default components to reduce the software that must be maintained and the tools available to an attacker after a container compromise.
  • It says security controls such as curated base images, runtime profiling, removal of unused components, vulnerability context, and automated rebuilding should be integrated into CI/CD so secure software delivery becomes the default path.

Technologies: container-platform, ci-cd

Products: rapidfort-curated-images, nginx

Vendors: rapidfort, nginx

item.title: Volant Manticore, VMware vCenter CVE-2026-123903, and AI-Assisted Attacks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 24 Nov 11:00 → 24 Nov 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

VMware vCenter Hit by Another Critical 9.8-Rated Auth Bypass Flaw After Zero-Day Exploitation — Must Read

Broadcom released patches for a critical VMware vCenter authentication-bypass flaw, CVE-2026-123903 (CVSS 9.8), which lets network-accessible attackers gain unauthorized access. Organizations should urgently update affected vCenter and VMware Cloud Foundation deployments, especially following a separate recently exploited vCenter zero-day.

  • Broadcom released patches for 23 vulnerabilities affecting VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion, and Avi Load Balancer.
  • CVE-2026-123903 is a critical VMware Directory Service flaw rated 9.8 that could allow an attacker with network access to vCenter to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized system access.
  • Broadcom also fixed CVE-2026-123904, a high-severity arbitrary file-write issue that could lead to code execution on the vCenter appliance, along with three Directory Service denial-of-service flaws.
  • Fixes are available for VMware Cloud Foundation and vSphere Foundation 9.1 and 9.0, vCenter 8.0, Cloud Foundation 5.x, and certain VMware Telco Cloud products; vCenter 7.0 customers on extended support must contact Broadcom Support.
  • Broadcom said CVE-2026-123903 is distinct from the recently exploited CVE-2026-123890 authentication-bypass zero-day, and did not report active exploitation of the newly disclosed flaws.

Technologies: hypervisor, load-balancer, cloud-platform, identity-provider

Products: vmware-vcenter, vmware-esx, vmware-workstation, vmware-fusion, vmware-avi-load-balancer, vmware-cloud-foundation, vmware-vsphere-foundation, vmware-directory-service, vmware-telco-cloud-platform, vmware-telco-cloud-infrastructure

Vendors: broadcom, vmware

Volant Manticore: Flying Under the Radar — Should Read

Check Point Research identified Volant Manticore, a likely Iran-linked espionage group with ties to former MuddyWater operators, targeting Cyprus and recently Saudi healthcare organizations. The group uses the IPFS-based KuboShell backdoor, the Homa framework, phishing, credential harvesting, and remote-management tools to gain and maintain access.

  • Check Point Research identified Volant Manticore as a previously undocumented Iran-nexus threat group that it assesses is historically linked to Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security and has multiple overlaps with MuddyWater.
  • Volant Manticore used fake CVs and healthcare-themed phishing archives to deliver the IPFS-based KuboShell backdoor, remote-management tools, and credential-harvesting infrastructure.
  • KuboShell uses Pinata’s IPFS pinning service for command-and-control, identifies hosts through their MAC addresses, executes received PowerShell commands, and polls for new commands every 60 seconds.
  • The group’s Homa Framework uses a multi-stage PowerShell and JavaScript infection chain whose third-stage client closely resembles MuddyWater’s older MuddyC2Go framework.
  • The group primarily targeted Cypriot telecommunications companies, airlines, and likely government entities before shifting toward Saudi Arabian targets, including healthcare organizations, in September 2026.

Technologies: remote-access, vpn, object-storage

Products: netlock-rmm, n-able-rmm, meshcentral, fortinet-ssl-vpn

Vendors: pinata, fortinet, n-able, meshcentral

Okta Links ShinyHunters-Associated Vishing Group to New INCEPTION Data Leak Site — Should Read

Okta says the ShinyHunters-associated O-UNC-053 vishing group appears to be using the new INCEPTION leak site to extort victims after stealing SaaS data through credential phishing and MFA approval scams. The group is actively registering target-specific legal-themed domains and remains a threat across multiple industries.

  • Okta assesses that O-UNC-053, a threat cluster previously associated with ShinyHunters, may have shifted to a new data leak site branded INCEPTION while continuing vishing-based account takeover and extortion activity.
  • O-UNC-053 operators call targeted users and socially engineer them into entering credentials on phishing pages, sharing one-time codes, or approving MFA push notifications, enabling access to SaaS applications and data theft.
  • Since October 2026, the group has used target-specific legal-themed domains such as legal-<target>.com and <target>-legal.com, often registering them on or within a day of a campaign starting.
  • Okta said targeted organizations' names appeared on the ShinyHunters leak site between one and 28 days after the phishing infrastructure was registered during activity observed from March through September 2026.
  • The article states that it remains unclear whether data posted on the INCEPTION site is authentic, whether O-UNC-053 operates the site itself, and what its exact relationship with ShinyHunters is.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, mfa

Products: okta-fastpass

Vendors: okta, cloudflare

Google Researcher Shows How a Single Bit Change in .NET Files Bypassed Windows Code Integrity — Should Read

Google Project Zero found that a .NET Framework loading quirk could bypass Oracle VirtualBox process hardening and Windows User Mode Code Integrity, including through a one-bit change to a .NET file header. Oracle and Microsoft have released fixes for CVE-2026-87268 and CVE-2026-108398, so affected VirtualBox and Windows/.NET installations should be updated.

  • Google Project Zero researcher James Forshaw found that a .NET Framework loading fallback could let locally run untrusted code bypass Oracle VirtualBox process hardening and Windows code-integrity protections.
  • The VirtualBox issue, CVE-2026-87268, affected Windows hosts and allowed AnyCPU .NET files to be loaded through a memory-based path that VirtualBox’s protections did not inspect.
  • For CVE-2026-108398, clearing the IMAGE_FILE_EXECUTABLE_IMAGE bit in a .NET file header caused Windows to reject it as an executable image while .NET Framework 4 could still load and run it, bypassing User Mode Code Integrity in testing on Windows 11 S Mode.
  • Oracle released fixes for the VirtualBox flaw in September, while Microsoft fixed the Windows code-integrity issue on October 13 and stated that it had not been used in attacks.
  • Forshaw also demonstrated loading code into the high-protection WerSecureFault.exe process through a COM object hijack, and stated that this Protected Process Light route should still work after Microsoft’s UMCI fix.

Technologies: hypervisor, operating-system

Products: oracle-vm-virtualbox, windows, net-framework, windows-11-s-mode

Vendors: oracle, microsoft, google-project-zero

McDonald’s Japan discloses breach exposing customer purchase and location data — Should Read

McDonald’s Japan disclosed unauthorized access to a database tied to its mobile app, potentially exposing customers’ purchase histories, IP addresses, internal IDs, and device location data. The company says names, payment details, and contact information were not affected, and the scope and cause remain under investigation.

  • McDonald’s Japan disclosed unauthorized access to a database associated with its official mobile app.
  • The potentially exposed data included customers’ purchase histories, IP addresses, internal customer identification numbers, and mobile-device location data.
  • McDonald’s Japan said names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, and credit card information were not affected.
  • The company has not disclosed how many customers were affected, when the intrusion occurred, how the attacker obtained credentials, or whether customer data was stolen.
  • McDonald’s Japan is investigating the affected systems, invalidating the credentials used in the incident, and has reported it to Japan’s data protection authorities.

Products: mcdonalds-mobile-app

Vendors: mcdonalds

UK cyber agency seeing ‘marked rise’ in AI-driven attacks — Optional

The UK’s NCSC reports a marked rise in AI-assisted cyberattacks, with agentic offensive frameworks enabling attackers to find and exploit existing weaknesses faster, more cheaply and at scale. The agency stresses that strong basic security controls remain the best defense because these tools do not introduce fundamentally new attack capabilities.

  • Britain’s National Cyber Security Centre said it has observed a marked rise in AI-assisted cyberattacks since September.
  • The NCSC said agentic offensive frameworks increase attackers’ speed, scale and persistence while reducing costs, using widely available hacking frameworks and inexpensive AI models or illicit API access.
  • The agency said the weaknesses being exploited are not new, and the AI tools do not provide capabilities unavailable to typical threat actors.
  • The NCSC identified Artex as the framework currently receiving the most attention and named Cairn, PentAGI, RedAmon, Xalgorix and Darkmoon as other examples.
  • The NCSC said strong basic security controls remain important because AI can make overlooked access keys and unprotected APIs easier to find and faster to exploit.

Products: artex, cairn, pentagi, redamon, xalgorix, darkmoon

2027 SOC Budget Reset: 5 Priorities to Cut Costs and Reduce Cyber Risk — Optional

South Korea’s state-controlled power utility KEPCO confirmed that attackers accessed its billing and procurement systems, exposing personal and financial information for more than 1.5 million customers, employees, and company representatives. A threat actor using the alias Noiem claimed responsibility, though attribution remains unconfirmed.

Organizations should treat every prompt as external data exposure, restrict provider routing, prevent credentials from entering agent context, and retain prompt audit trails for incident response.

  • Dragos researchers embedded unique trackable secrets in about two million prompts sent to widely used AI services and reported that prompts were retained, shared with other companies, and read by people.

Hardened container images: STIGs, FIPS and FedRAMP explained — Optional

Hardened container images reduce attack surface by removing unnecessary components and enforcing secure configurations against baselines such as DISA STIGs, while FIPS separately governs use of validated cryptographic modules. FedRAMP requires hardened, regularly scanned images and pipeline enforcement, but these practices benefit any organization seeking stronger container security.

  • A hardened container image removes software the application does not need, such as shells, package managers, and compilers, and locks down the remaining configuration.
  • DISA STIGs are U.S. Department of Defense configuration standards with individual checks that can be tested and documented, including checks that do not apply to containers because they are handled by the host.
  • FIPS 140 concerns validated cryptographic modules and does not by itself harden a container image or ensure that every application component uses approved cryptography.
  • FedRAMP requires container images to be hardened against a benchmark from NIST’s National Checklist Program, scanned before deployment, and assessed within the previous 30 days before running in production.
  • Minimal, distroless, and scratch images can reduce attack surface, but they do not necessarily meet a defined secure-configuration baseline.

Technologies: container-platform, operating-system, ci-cd

AI and autonomous agents dramatically increase traffic, operational dependency, and security risks, but SASE’s core distributed, edge-delivered zero-trust architecture remains the right foundation. Webworm Suspected of Modifying SoftEther VPN to Evade Detection and Hide Remote Access — Should Read

China-aligned Webworm is suspected of rebuilding SoftEther VPN Bridge as “NtMonitor VPN” to remove recognizable fingerprints and conceal covert remote access. The modified tool changes HTTP endpoints, handshake watermarks, and configuration storage for stealth rather than adding new capabilities.

  • Rapid7 assessed with moderate confidence that the China-aligned Webworm group is using a modified build of SoftEther VPN Bridge to conceal remote access to compromised networks.
  • The Windows executable netcapa.exe is based on SoftEther VPN Bridge version 4.44 build 9807 and is rebranded as “NtMonitor VPN,” presenting itself as Network Monitor Software.
  • The altered tool replaces SoftEther’s usual HTTP endpoints and GIF-based handshake marker with ordinary-looking endpoints and a PNG-based marker to evade detection signatures.
  • The modified build renames and encrypts its configuration file as setting.conf, which begins with the ASCII magic bytes “RCEN.”
  • Rapid7 found no new functionality in the modified tool, indicating that its changes are focused on stealth rather than added capabilities.

item.content:encoded:

Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning — Must Read

Attackers are actively exploiting the critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect flaw CVE-2026-84869 to silently push and execute malicious files on MSP technicians’ workstations, enabling remote takeover and access to customer environments. Organizations should update ScreenConnect host clients to version 26.6.5 or later and investigate potentially exposed technician systems.

  • Threat actors are exploiting CVE-2026-84869, a critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect client flaw with a CVSS score of 9.9, to transfer and execute files on a connecting technician’s host.
  • Huntress observed an MSP technician workstation run a guest-pushed batch file that contacted a Telegram bot, downloaded a Windows-update-themed MSI installer, and launched a rogue ScreenConnect client within about nine seconds.
  • Between October 20 and November 16, 2026, Huntress recorded at least 688,000 guest “run file” requests targeting 42 ScreenConnect servers from 29 IP addresses.
  • Huntress also identified 2,408 unauthorized ScreenConnect guest sessions across at least 118 self-hosted servers belonging to 109 protected organizations, with many using cryptocurrency exchange-themed names.
  • Organizations are advised to update technician ScreenConnect host clients to version 26.6.5 or later, or remove the TransferFiles permission if patching cannot occur immediately.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: screenconnect, screenconnect-access, sckit

Vendors: connectwise, huntress, telegram, ionos

N-able Discloses Critical Mail Assure Vulnerability Found During Breach Investigation — Should Read

N-able fixed a critical SSRF flaw (CVE-2026-134624) in its Mail Assure/SpamExperts Hosted Cloud platform after investigating an unauthorized server access incident. The company says no customer data compromise has been found, but customers must replace revoked API and OAuth credentials.

  • N-able disclosed CVE-2026-134624, a critical server-side request forgery flaw in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud email-filtering service.
  • The flaw allowed authenticated users with high-level API access to make the platform connect to chosen internal hosts and ports and send crafted data to internal services.
  • N-able patched the issue in build 20261121.1943 and restored dashboard and API access late Saturday after an outage that began the previous Monday.
  • During the incident response, N-able took an affected Hosted Cloud server offline, rotated internal credentials, revoked customer API and OAuth tokens, and reset local user passwords.
  • N-able says it has found no evidence of customer-data compromise or exploitation beyond one server, and its investigation remains ongoing.

Technologies: email-security, network-monitoring

Products: mail-assure, spamexperts-hosted-cloud, spamexperts-local-cloud, n-central

Vendors: n-able

Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions — Should Read

Binary-parser versions before 2.3.1 have a critical code-injection flaw (CVE-2026-134814) that can let attackers who control parser definitions execute arbitrary JavaScript in Node.js during parser compilation. Users should upgrade to version 2.3.1 or later.

  • Binary-parser versions before 2.3.1 contain CVE-2026-134814, a code-injection flaw that can allow arbitrary JavaScript execution when an attacker controls parser definitions.
  • The flaw stems from string options such as length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, and aliases passed to namely() being inserted into generated JavaScript without adequate validation.
  • The vulnerability is triggered when a crafted parser definition is compiled in a Node.js process, not simply by parsing untrusted binary data with a trusted parser definition.
  • The binary-parser maintainer stated that version 2.3.1 validates these options as identifier paths and rejects expressions such as "len - 1."
  • CVE-2026-134814 is described as an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-1245, an earlier code-injection issue involving insufficient validation of field names and encoding parameters.

Products: binary-parser, node-js

Vendors: binary-parser, github, nist
